title: Sign every handshake with the key of the certificate it sent

blocks.text: This practice continues the previous one: `TlsCredentials` now keeps the certificate and its key together, and a reload replaces them safely. The listener also needs the server's side of a handshake, which sends the certificate to the client and then signs with the private key; the client checks the signature against the certificate it received.

Finish `serve(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/TlsCredentials.java`. Reloads keep happening on the reload thread while handshakes run, and a reload can complete between the two steps of a handshake. When you're done, every handshake signs with the key of the certificate it sent, and the handshakes after a reload use the renewed pair. About three lines in total.
The tests complete a reload on another thread right after the certificate is sent.

cases.says: a handshake sends the current certificate and signs with its key, before and after a reload
a reload that completes after the certificate was sent doesn't change the key the same handshake signs with

origin.section: Every Read of a volatile Field Can See a New Value: Read It Once per Decision

concepts: Each read of a volatile field can see a new value, so a decision that uses the value more than once reads the field once into a local.
